srv-07.detail: The member made no change, as the item required. AppQyV1TtsEngineConfigModel::seedDefaults (:85-110) is ensure-only: it collects the missing DEFAULT_ENGINES rows, runs insertOrIgnore on them, and returns updated 0. The upsert of priority_order is in 5bbb23682, not in G1. The member's seed_verify.php was re-run inside a rolled-back PG transaction (connection appqyv1, pgsql). Setting kokoro to priority 99 and enabled false, then seeding, gave {seeded:0,updated:0}, and both values stayed. Deleting sherpa, then seeding, gave {seeded:1,updated:0}, and sherpa was re-inserted. After the rollback kokoro was back at 8/true. sys:init was not run.

srv-07b.detail: AppQyV1TtsVariantSpecModel::seedDefaults (:99-132) is ensure-only. It reads (lang, variant_key, is_primary) for the default languages, builds only the missing default rows with created_at/updated_at, runs insertOrIgnore (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on uniq_tts_variant_spec_lang_key), and returns updated 0. Existing rows are never written. The choice to insert a missing default primary as non-primary when the language already has a primary matches the one-primary rule in replaceForLanguage (:193-224). The re-run in a rolled-back transaction passed every case. (1) en/uk_f set to male/au/primary and en/'' set to non-primary, then seeded: {0,0}, and every edit stayed. (2) ja/m deleted, then seeded: {1,0}, and it was re-inserted as male and non-primary. (3) en/'' deleted while uk_f is primary, then seeded: {1,0}; the re-inserted row is non-primary, and en has exactly 1 primary. After the rollback the rows were at their originals.

MCHR-27.detail: LibraryPublicController::transformLibrary (:815) now uses presentCover(), and getCoverData is unchanged. The g1_verify.php re-run through the in-process HTTP kernel with a QueryExecuted listener gave these results. GET /api/app_qy_v1/vocabulary/libraries?per_page=50: 200, 8 rows, 2 queries, 0 UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE. GET /libraries/recommended: 200, 7 rows, 2 queries, 0 writes. The 21 keys are unchanged, every row has cover_task, and every cover_url carries ?v=. Through the live worker, GET :9000/api/app_qy_v1/vocabulary/libraries returned 200. LDRI-22.detail: purgeExpired is public, returns int, and register() still calls it (:80). Selection groups files per 40-hex batch id (BATCH_FILE_PATTERN :53, which also catches .tmp staging files), prefilters on every file's mtime, and then decides by stored state. The count covers only fully deleted batches. The purge_verify.php re-run with a sudo.bat shim returned 3 and then 0. It removed done-old, awaiting-old and orphan-bin-old. It kept processing-old, done with a fresh state, awaiting-fresh and README.txt. It returned 0 natively on HEAD, and 3 natively once pycore-laravel's in-flight deleteNative is in the working tree. Worker restart and /api/health are 200. Defect: batchExpired (:362-375) keeps every processing batch forever, whatever its age. A processing batch only stops being processing when advance() runs, and advance() runs only in the deferred call or in a status() poll. If the worker dies mid-advance (a FrankenPHP worker restart is enough) and pycore never polls that batch again, for example because a new diff produces a different batch id, its state, lock and up to MAX_TOTAL_BYTES (32 MB) of .bin content are never purged. The old mtime purge removed them after 24 h, so this is a regression. It is also no longer 'running': a live batch checkpoints its state every CHECKPOINT_ITEMS items (:213-217), and a status poll resumes it after STALE_PROCESSING_SECONDS. The report (line 111) hands this to the pycore-laravel timer. The agreed API, purgeExpired(): int, cannot reach it, so it must be fixed in the service half.

issues: LDRI-22 (AppQyV1DeliveryBatchService.php:361-375 batchExpired, docblock :329-334): expire abandoned processing batches too. Use the same rule as done/awaiting_content: every file is older than RETENTION_SECONDS AND the stored updated_at is older than the cutoff. Such a batch cannot be live, because advance() checkpoints its state every CHECKPOINT_ITEMS items and a status poll resumes it after STALE_PROCESSING_SECONDS. Purging it loses nothing permanent: items already stored stay, and missing ones are re-offered by pycore's index-driven diff delivery through the fill-missing writers. Recommended form: drop the STATE_PROCESSING exception, so the rule reads `return $state === null || (int) ($state['updated_at'] ?? 0) < $cutoff;`. Keep the API as public function purgeExpired(): int. Update the docblock, and remove the 'processing batch ... stays until a status poll' caveat from reports/wordnew-laravel.md (line 111). Verify with purge_verify.php plus two cases. (a) processing with updated_at 2 days old and all mtimes old: removed. (b) processing with updated_at = now and old mtimes: kept. The expected return is 4, then 0 on the second call. Run it with the sudo.bat shim, or natively when pycore-laravel's FileSystemManager::deleteNative is present. Then run php -l, restart the FrankenPHP workers (curl -X POST http://localhost:2019/frankenphp/workers/restart), and check that GET http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/health returns 200.

non_blocking: srv-07b design note for wordnew-lead (not a member defect, because the item's verify requires re-insertion): replaceForLanguage deletes and recreates a language's specs. So an operator who removes a default voice (for example en/us_m, to get 2 voices) gets it back at the next sys:init. Specs have no enabled flag, unlike engines. A per-language ensure would respect removals: seed a language only when it has no rows. That change needs a ruling first, because it changes what 'missing' means for srv-07.

LDRI-28: ImageFileProcessor :315 does one index put per imported image during sys:init. That is fine with RedisBucketIndex's cached availability and single-HSET puts. If bulk imports grow, batch the puts or rely on rebuild afterwards.

MCHR-27 follow-on: the comments in app/Services/TimerTasks/AppQyV1CoverGenerationTask.php (:102-106, :176-185) still say that list rendering initializes cover_* through getCoverData, and after this change it does not. That file is pycore-laravel's, so this is a comment-only fix for its owner.

LDRI-22: purgeExpired may delete a stale batch in the same instant that a late status poll starts advancing it. The window is tiny, and the effect is benign (the items are reported invalid and pycore re-delivers them). A non-blocking FileSystemManager::runWithExclusiveFileLock around the per-batch delete would close it, but it is optional.
